mainTopic: How a communal פסח is brought בטומאה (only for טומאת מת), whether a מצורע gets מלקות for entering a forbidden camp, and the three camps for impure people
overview: This amud opens with the end of ריש לקיש's proof that when most of the people are טמא מת, the קרבן פסח is still brought בטומאה. He reads the extra mention of זבין and מצורעים in the verse about sending impure people out of the camp as hinting to a פסח הבא בטומאה. אביי shows that the same method would let זבין take part, which a משנה forbids. So אביי goes back to רבי יוחנן's verse. There, the word איש teaches that an individual is pushed off to פסח שני. The word לנפש teaches that a ציבור brings the פסח בטומאה only when the impurity is טומאת מת. Next, רב חסדא rules that a מצורע who enters a forbidden camp gets no מלקות, because the Torah turned his לאו into an עשה. A ברייתא says he gets ארבעים, and the גמרא answers that this is a dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, with רב חסדא following רבי שמעון. Finally, the גמרא tests רבי שמעון's claim that a זב is more severe than a טמא מת and a טמא שרץ. The answer to the last challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's conclusion: טמאי מתים are not sent out for a פסח brought בטומאה
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש finishes his derivation. The verse's extra mention of זבין and מצורעים teaches that at a פסח הבא בטומאה, זבין and מצורעים are still excluded, but טמאי מתים are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the verse teaches that there is a time when זבין and מצורעים are sent out, but טמאי מתים are not sent out. When is that? When a פסח is brought in a state of impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes ריש לקיש's proof. The verse mentions זבין and מצורעים even though they were not needed. That extra mention teaches that there is a special time when only טמאי מתים may stay: a פסח brought בטומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, ריש לקיש argued that the verse only needed to mention טמאי מתים. If even they are sent out, then זבין and מצורעים, whose impurity is stricter, would be sent out all the more so. Since the Torah mentions זבין and מצורעים anyway, the extra words teach a new rule: there is a time when they are sent out and טמאי מתים are not. When the community is impure from the dead, the פסח is brought anyway, and טמאי מתים take part. זבין and מצורעים still stay out.

keyTerms.meaning: People impure because of a bodily discharge (זב)
People with צרעת, a severe form of impurity
People impure from contact with a dead body
Are sent out of the camp
A קרבן פסח brought while the community is impure

steps.whyThisMatters: This is ריש לקיש's whole source for the rule that טומאת מת is set aside for a communal פסח. The rest of this passage tests whether his method holds up.

phrases.english: Rather, you have a time
when zavin and lepers are sent out
but those impure from a corpse are not sent out,
and which time is this?
phrases.notes: This question just sets up the answer that comes next.

phrases.english: A Paschal offering brought in impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes ריש לקיש's derivation, which began earlier
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a פסח is brought בטומאה, טמאי מתים take part, but זבין and מצורעים are still excluded.

steps.title: אביי: the same logic would make the leper the only one excluded
steps.stepSummary: אביי applies ריש לקיש's method to the mention of מצורע. By that logic, the verse would be teaching that at a פסח הבא בטומאה only מצורעים are sent out, and זבין may stay.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: If so, we should also say this. The verse could have mentioned only זב and טמאי מתים, and left out מצורע. I would know on my own that if a זב is sent out, a מצורע certainly is. So the extra mention of מצורע must teach that there is a time when only מצורעים are sent out, and זבין and טמאי מתים are not. That time is a פסח brought בטומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges ריש לקיש by using his own method against him. If an extra word teaches a special exception, then the extra word מצורע should also teach an exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מצורע is more impure than a זב, so mentioning מצורע seems unnecessary. A קל וחומר from זב would already tell us he is sent out. Following ריש לקיש's logic, that extra mention would teach that even זבין may take part in a פסח הבא בטומאה. אביי is setting up a result that he will show is false.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, a formula for showing where an argument leads
Let us also say
And I would say, meaning I could derive it myself
All the more so, the language of a קל וחומר

phrases.english: Abaye said: If so,

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא נָמֵי: יֵאָמֵר זָב וּטְמֵאֵי מֵתִים,
phrases.english: let us also say: let it mention zav and those impure from a corpse,
and let it not mention a leper,
and I would say: if a zav is sent out,
then a leper, is it not all the more so?

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: יֵשׁ לְךָ שָׁעָה שֶׁמְּצוֹרָעִין מִשְׁתַּלְּחִין,
phrases.english: Rather, you have a time when lepers are sent out,
but zavin and those impure from a corpse are not sent out,
and which time is this?
A Paschal offering brought in impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אִי הָכִי, לֵימָא נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the method of derivation used in step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's method of reading an unnecessary item in the verse as a hint to a פסח הבא בטומאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same method, applied to the unnecessary mention of מצורע, would mean זבין may take part in a פסח הבא בטומאה. Step 3 shows this is false.

steps.title: A משנה proves זבים may not eat from a פסח brought בטומאה
steps.stepSummary: Someone might simply accept that זבין may take part. אביי blocks this with a משנה that says זבים, זבות, נדות, and יולדות may not eat from a פסח הבא בטומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that this is indeed true, don't we have a משנה? It says that from a פסח brought בטומאה, זבים, זבות, נדות, and יולדות may not eat. But if they did eat, they are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shuts the escape route. One could not answer "yes, זבין really may join," because a משנה clearly says they may not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 showed that ריש לקיש's method leads to the result that זבין may take part. This משנה proves that result is wrong. So the method itself must be flawed, and ריש לקיש's derivation is undermined.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say that it is indeed so
Menstruating women and women after childbirth, whose impurity is like a זב's
Exempt, here meaning not liable to כרת

steps.confusionAlert: פטורין does not mean they are allowed to eat. From the start, they may not eat. The word only means that if they did eat, they are not punished with כרת.

phrases.english: And if you say that it is indeed so,
but didn't we learn: a Paschal offering brought in impurity,
they may not eat from it:
zavim and zavot, menstruating women and women after childbirth,
and if they ate, they are exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's challenge by proving that the result reached in step 2 is false
steps.kashyaTarget: The possible defense that זבין really may take part in a פסח הבא בטומאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה explicitly excludes זבים and similar impurities, so the result of ריש לקיש's method contradicts an established law.
steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש's reading of the verse about sending people out of the camp fails. Used consistently, it would allow זבין at a פסח הבא בטומאה, and the משנה forbids that.

steps.title: אביי returns to רבי יוחנן's verse and asks why it says 'by reason of a corpse'
steps.stepSummary: אביי concludes that the source must come from the first verse, רבי יוחנן's verse: איש איש כי יהיה טמא לנפש. He asks why the word לנפש is needed, which sets up a new derivation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: Actually, the source is the first verse. If that verse only came to teach that an individual is pushed off to פסח שני and the community is not, the Torah could have written just "any man who shall be impure." Why do I need the words "by reason of a corpse"?
steps.whatsHappening: With ריש לקיש's source rejected, אביי goes back to רבי יוחנן's verse. He asks why the extra word לנפש is there. This step is setting up his answer, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי יוחנן's reading, the words איש איש show that only an individual is deferred to פסח שני, and not the ציבור. If that were all, the Torah would not need to say which kind of impurity is meant. So the word לנפש must be teaching something specific about טומאת מת. אביי will use that extra word to build the source.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really; returning to an earlier position
From the first verse, meaning רבי יוחנן's verse
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
By reason of a soul, meaning a corpse
Why do I need it? A sign that a word seems unnecessary

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
Actually, it is from the first verse.
If so, let the Merciful One write:
"Any man who shall be impure";
why do I need "by reason of a corpse"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לְעוֹלָם מִקְּרָא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ריש לקיש's verse is rejected in steps 2 and 3, אביי goes back to רבי יוחנן's verse and opens a new reading of it
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The source is רבי יוחנן's verse. The seemingly extra word לנפש is the key to the derivation, which is explained next.

steps.title: A first suggestion: לנפש means only a טמא מת gets פסח שני
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the word לנפש teaches that only someone impure from a dead body is pushed off to פסח שני, and other impure people are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that this word לנפש comes to teach this: only someone impure from a dead body is pushed off to פסח שני, but other impure people are not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer to אביי's question about why the Torah wrote לנפש. This is a test idea, and the גמרא will knock it down right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion reads לנפש as a limit on who may bring פסח שני: only a טמא מת, and not a זב or a מצורע. If this were right, the word would have nothing to do with a פסח הבא בטומאה. The opening words וכי תימא signal that a rejection is coming.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say. Introduces a possible idea that is about to be rejected.
By reason of a dead body (נֶפֶשׁ here means a corpse)
The second פסח, a month later, for those who missed the first one
Is pushed off, is deferred

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up two different situations. פסח שני is a make-up date one month later for people who could not bring the first פסח. A פסח הבא בטומאה is a first פסח brought on time even though people are impure. The question is which of these two the word לנפש is talking about.

phrases.english: And if you say
that this word 'by reason of a corpse' comes for this purpose:
phrases.notes: The suggested job of the word לנפש.

phrases.aramaic: הַטְּמֵא מֵת הוּא דְּנִדְחֶה לְפֶסַח שֵׁנִי,
phrases.english: it is the one impure from a corpse who is pushed off to the second Pesach,
but other impure people are not.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הַאי לָנֶפֶשׁ לְהָכִי הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to אביי's question about why לנפש is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the word to a different law (who gets פסח שני)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: לנפש seems to have no job, so maybe it limits פסח שני to a טמא מת.
steps.terutzMaskana: This is only a passing idea. A ברייתא will reject it in the next step.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows all impure people get פסח שני, so why write לנפש?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from איש איש that זבין, מצורעים, and בועלי נדות also bring פסח שני. So the suggestion fails, and the question returns: why does the Torah need the word לנפש?
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא taught: I might think that only people impure from a dead body, and someone who was on a far journey, bring פסח שני. From where do we know that זבין, מצורעים, and men who were with a נדה also do? The verse says 'איש איש' (any man). So why did the Torah write לנפש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that disproves the suggestion in step 5. Then it asks again why the Torah needed the word לנפש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the doubled word איש איש includes every kind of impure person for פסח שני. So לנפש cannot be limiting פסח שני to a טמא מת. The word לנפש is back to having no clear job.

keyTerms.meaning: A far journey. A person too far away to bring the first פסח.
Men who had relations with a נדה and became impure from it
The verse teaches. Introduces the verse used as the source.
Any man. The doubled word is read as including more people.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל לֹא יְהוּ עוֹשִׂין פֶּסַח שֵׁנִי
phrases.english: One might think that none would bring the second Pesach

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא טְמֵאֵי מֵתִים וְשֶׁהָיָה בְּדֶרֶךְ רְחוֹקָה,
phrases.english: except those impure from a corpse and one who was on a distant journey;
from where do we know to include zavin, lepers, and those who had relations with menstruating women?
The verse states: 'Any man,'
phrases.notes: The doubled word includes all kinds of impure people.

phrases.english: So why do I need 'by reason of a corpse' that the Merciful One wrote?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 5 and brings back the question of step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that לנפש limits פסח שני to a טמא מת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא learns from איש איש that every kind of impure person brings פסח שני. So לנפש cannot be teaching that limit, and it still has no job.

steps.title: The real meaning: an individual is pushed off, but an impure community brings the פסח only in טומאת מת
steps.stepSummary: The verse means that one person is pushed off to פסח שני, but a whole community brings the first פסח in טומאה. The word לנפש teaches that this works only when the impurity is טומאת מת, not other kinds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what the verse means: an individual is pushed off to פסח שני, but the community is not pushed off to פסח שני. Instead, they bring the פסח while impure. And when the community brings it while impure, that is with impurity from a dead body. With other kinds of impurity, they do not bring it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final answer about why the Torah wrote לנפש. This finishes the source אביי was looking for in step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word איש (an individual) tells us that only a single person is pushed off. When the ציבור is impure, they bring the פסח on time, in טומאה. The word לנפש limits that permission to טומאת מת. This explains the משנה from step 3: זבים and others may not eat from a פסח הבא בטומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, this is what it means. Introduces a new reading of the source.
The community, meaning all or most of the people
They bring the קרבן while impure
Other kinds of impurity, such as זב or מצורע

steps.whatToRemember: An individual who is impure goes to פסח שני. A community that is impure brings the first פסח in טומאה, but only when the impurity is טומאת מת. The word לנפש is the source for that limit. So זבין and מצורעים are left out of a פסח הבא בטומאה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answers the long search that started with ריש לקיש. The exclusion of זבין and מצורעים from a פסח הבא בטומאה comes from רבי יוחנן's verse, through the word לנפש.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what it is saying:
an individual is pushed off to the second Pesach,
but the community is not pushed off to the second Pesach;
rather, they perform it in impurity.
And when the community performs it in impurity —
that is with corpse impurity,
phrases.notes: This is the job of the word לנפש.

phrases.english: but with other impurities, they do not perform it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 with a new reading of the verse.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the verse: איש teaches about the individual versus the community, and לנפש limits which impurity is allowed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: לנפש seemed to have no job, since איש איש includes every impure person for פסח שני.
steps.terutzMaskana: לנפש teaches that a community may bring the פסח in טומאה only when the impurity is טומאת מת.

steps.title: רב חסדא: a מצורע who enters a forbidden area gets no lashes
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that a מצורע who goes into an area forbidden to him is פטור from מלקות. His source is the verse בדד ישב מחוץ למחנה מושבו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: A מצורע who went inside his boundary is פטור, as it says: 'He shall dwell alone; his dwelling shall be outside the camp.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new but related topic: impure people who must be sent out of the camps. רב חסדא gives a ruling about a מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an impure person who enters a forbidden camp gets מלקות for breaking ולא יטמאו את מחניהם. רב חסדא says a מצורע is different and is פטור from מלקות. He still did something forbidden; he just does not get lashes. The reason is in the verse, explained in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with צרעת, who must stay outside all the camps
Inside his boundary, meaning into an area forbidden to him
Exempt. Here it means exempt from מלקות.
He shall dwell alone

steps.confusionAlert: פטור here does not mean it is allowed. It means he does not get מלקות.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
A leper who entered inside his boundary
phrases.notes: He went into an area forbidden to him.

phrases.english: is exempt,
as it is stated: 'He shall dwell alone;
his dwelling shall be outside the camp.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, linked to the earlier verses about sending impure people out of the camp.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מצורע who enters a forbidden area does not get מלקות.

steps.title: Explaining the verse: the Torah turned the prohibition into a positive command
steps.stepSummary: בדד ישב means the מצורע lives alone. מחוץ למחנה מושבו shows that the Torah made his prohibition into a לאו הניתק לעשה, so he gets no מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He shall dwell alone' means he lives by himself. 'His dwelling shall be outside the camp' means the verse turned the prohibition into a positive command.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רב חסדא's verse proves his ruling. This finishes his teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words בדד ישב teach that a מצורע lives alone, not even with other impure people. The words מחוץ למחנה מושבו give him a positive command: if he went in, he must go back out. Because his לאו can be fixed by doing a עשה, there is no מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: By himself, alone
Turned it into a positive command
A prohibition that can be fixed by doing a positive command. It does not get מלקות.

steps.whatToRemember: A מצורע who enters a forbidden area is פטור from מלקות. The Torah turned his לאו into an עשה, telling him to go back out, and a לאו הניתק לעשה does not get lashes.

phrases.english: 'He shall dwell alone' — he shall live by himself.
phrases.notes: Not even together with other impure people.

phrases.english: 'His dwelling shall be outside the camp' —
the verse has turned it into a positive command.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the verse quoted by רב חסדא proves his ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מחוץ למחנה מושבו makes the מצורע's prohibition a לאו הניתק לעשה, so he is פטור from מלקות.

steps.title: A ברייתא says a מצורע who enters gets lashes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא from a ברייתא. It says a מצורע who goes past his boundary gets ארבעים lashes, and so do זבין and זבות. A טמא מת may enter the מחנה לויה, and even a dead body may be brought there, as we see from משה taking יוסף's bones 'with him'.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: A מצורע who went inside past his boundary gets forty lashes. זבין and זבות who went inside past their boundary get forty lashes. A טמא מת is allowed to enter the מחנה לויה. And they did not say this only about a טמא מת, but even about a dead body itself. As it says, 'And משה took the bones of יוסף with him.' 'With him' means inside his area.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that directly contradicts רב חסדא. רב חסדא said a מצורע is פטור from lashes, but this ברייתא says he gets ארבעים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said the מצורע's prohibition is a לאו הניתק לעשה, so it carries no lashes. The ברייתא's very first line says a מצורע who enters gets forty lashes. The rest of the ברייתא, about זבין, טמא מת, and יוסף's bones, explains which camp each type of טומאה may enter. The challenge comes from the first line.

keyTerms.meaning: Boundary, the area a person is allowed to be in
With forty, meaning the standard Torah punishment of מלקות (in practice 39 lashes)
Men and women who are impure from a bodily discharge
The Levite camp, the middle camp around the משכן
The bones (coffin) of יוסף, which traveled with בני ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: Only the first line (מצורע gets ארבעים) contradicts רב חסדא. The lines about טמא מת and יוסף's bones are part of the same ברייתא, but they are not the point of the challenge.

phrases.english: They raised an objection against him:
A leper who went in beyond his boundary
is punished with forty lashes.
Zavin and zavot who went in beyond their boundaries
are punished with forty lashes.

phrases.aramaic: וּטְמֵא מֵת מוּתָּר לִיכָּנֵס לְמַחֲנֵה לְוִיָּה.
phrases.english: And one impure from a corpse is permitted to enter the Levite camp.
And they did not say this only about one impure from a corpse,
but even about a corpse itself,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה אֶת עַצְמוֹת יוֹסֵף עִמּוֹ״
phrases.english: as it is stated: “And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him”
“with him” means within his boundary!
phrases.notes: משה was a לוי, so the bones were in the Levite camp

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב חסדא's ruling from Steps 8-9 that a מצורע is פטור from lashes.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that a מצורע who enters a forbidden area does not get מלקות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא openly states that a מצורע who enters past his boundary gets ארבעים, which is the opposite of רב חסדא's ruling.

steps.title: It is a dispute of תנאים: רבי יהודה's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the question of lashes depends on a dispute between תנאים. It brings רבי יהודה's view first. בדד ישב teaches that the מצורע sits apart from other impure people. ולא יטמאו את מחניהם teaches that זבין and טמאי מתים also get separate camps.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a dispute between תנאים, as a ברייתא teaches: 'בדד ישב' means he sits alone, so other impure people do not sit with him. You might think זבין and טמאי מתים are sent to the same camp. So the verse says 'and they shall not defile their camps' (plural), to give one camp to this one and another camp to that one. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב חסדא. It says he is not alone, because the issue is a dispute between תנאים, and it starts quoting the ברייתא with רבי יהודה's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reads בדד ישב as teaching only that the מצורע sits apart from other impure people. He learns the separate camps from the plural מחניהם. He does not read the verse as turning the לאו into an עשה, so in his view a מצורע who enters gets מלקות, like the challenging ברייתא. The other side, רבי שמעון, comes in steps 12-14, and he is the one רב חסדא follows.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
One might have thought
Therefore the verse says (to teach otherwise)
Their camps. The plural form teaches that there is more than one camp

steps.confusionAlert: The link to lashes only becomes explicit at the end of רבי שמעון's words (step 14), where he says בדד ישב turns the לאו into an עשה. רבי יהודה's view matches the ברייתא that gives ארבעים. It does not match רב חסדא.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of tanna'im, as it was taught:
“He shall dwell in isolation” means he shall dwell alone,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ טְמֵאִין אֲחֵרִים יוֹשְׁבִין עִמּוֹ.
phrases.english: so that other impure people should not dwell with him.
One might think that zavin and those impure from a corpse
are sent out to one camp.
Therefore the verse states: “and they shall not defile their camps,”
to give a camp for this one and a camp for that one,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from Step 10 by showing that רב חסדא follows one side of a dispute between תנאים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute between תנאים: the challenging ברייתא follows one תנא, and רב חסדא follows another.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא giving lashes to a מצורע is the only view, so רב חסדא is refuted.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא giving a מצורע ארבעים follows רבי יהודה. רב חסדא follows רבי שמעון, who says the verse turned the לאו into an עשה (step 14).

steps.title: רבי שמעון learns the second camp from the word זב
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says we do not need ולא יטמאו to teach separate camps. The verse lists צרוע, זב, and טמא לנפש. If a טמא מת is sent out, then a זב, whose impurity is more severe, would obviously be sent out too. So the extra word זב teaches that he gets a second camp.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: That is not needed. The verse says: 'They shall send out of the camp every צרוע, every זב, and everyone impure by a corpse.' The verse could have said only 'impure by a corpse' and left out זב. I would then reason: if those impure from a corpse are sent out, then all the more so זבין. So why does it say זב? To give him a second camp.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents the other side of the dispute between תנאים. רבי שמעון finds the separate camps in a different verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון uses a כל שכן argument. A זב is more impure than a טמא מת, so the Torah did not need to mention him. The extra mention therefore teaches a stricter law: a זב is excluded from an additional camp. רבי שמעון will end by reading בדד ישב as turning the מצורע's לאו into an עשה (step 14), which fits רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed (that source is unnecessary)
A person afflicted with צרעת (a מצורע)
Is it not all the more so? A קל וחומר-style argument
A second camp, an additional area the זב may not enter

steps.whatToRemember: There are three camps: the מצורע is excluded from the most, the זב from two, and the טמא מת from only the innermost. רבי יהודה learns this from ולא יטמאו את מחניהם, and רבי שמעון learns it from the extra words זב and מצורע. רב חסדא's 'no lashes' fits רבי שמעון. The ברייתא's 'ארבעים' fits רבי יהודה.
steps.whyThisMatters: The dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון about the source of the camps is also where the two views on מלקות for a מצורע come from. רבי שמעון's view, which ends in step 14, is the one רב חסדא follows.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: It is not necessary,
for surely it says:
“That they send out from the camp every leper
and every zav and anyone impure by a corpse,”

phrases.aramaic: יֵאָמֵר טְמֵאֵי מֵת וְאַל יֵאָמֵר טְמֵאֵי זָב,
phrases.english: Let it say those impure from a corpse and not say those impure as a zav,
and I would say: if those impure from a corpse are sent out,
zavin, is it not all the more so?
Why then is zav stated?
To give him a second camp.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing תנא's source for separate camps, completing the dispute cited in Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זב is excluded from a second camp, learned from the extra word זב by a כל שכן argument. So ולא יטמאו is not needed for the camps.

steps.title: The extra word מצורע gives a third camp
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון continues. If a זב must be sent out, a מצורע obviously must be too. So the word מצורע in the verse is extra, and it teaches that the מצורע gets a third camp.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse could have mentioned only a זב and not a מצורע. I would figure out the rest myself: if זבין are sent out, then מצורעין certainly are. So why does the verse mention מצורע? To give him a third camp.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון uses the same reasoning a second time. Now he moves from the זב up to the מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12, the extra word זב gave the זב a second camp. Here the same logic works one level higher. A מצורע's impurity is even more severe than a זב's, so mentioning him is not needed just to send him out. Therefore the word must teach something new: a third camp that is forbidden only to him.

keyTerms.meaning: are sent out (of the camp)
all the more so; obviously
a third camp
why was it stated? (it must teach something extra)

phrases.english: Let it say 'zav' and not say 'metzora',
and I would say on my own:
if zavin are sent out,
are metzoraim not all the more so?
Why then is 'metzora' stated?
To give him a third camp.
phrases.notes: The three camps are מחנה שכינה, מחנה לויה, and מחנה ישראל. The מצורע is sent out of all three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the 'extra word' logic of step 12, now moving from זב to מצורע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word מצורע is not needed to send him out, so it teaches that he is sent out of a third camp.

steps.title: So בדד ישב makes it a positive command, which fits רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון ends by saying that the verse בדד ישב turns the מצורע's prohibition into a עשה. So the מצורע gets no מלקות, just as רב חסדא said.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the verse says 'He shall dwell alone,' the Torah has turned the prohibition into a positive command.
steps.whatsHappening: This line closes the answer to the challenge from step 10. It shows that רב חסדא follows רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה read בדד ישב only as keeping other impure people away from the מצורע, and learned the camps from מחניהם. רבי שמעון reads the verse as turning the מצורע's prohibition into a לאו הניתק לעשה, which means no מלקות. The ברייתא that gave ארבעים lashes follows רבי יהודה, so it is no problem for רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: turned it into a positive command
a prohibition that is fixed by doing a positive command; it does not bring מלקות

steps.whatToRemember: The question of lashes depends on the תנאים. For רבי יהודה, the מצורע gets מלקות. For רבי שמעון, he gets none, and רב חסדא follows him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the תירוץ of step 11 and saves רב חסדא's ruling from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: When it says 'He shall dwell alone' —
the verse has turned it into a positive command.
phrases.notes: So there are no lashes, which matches רב חסדא.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר בָּדָד יֵשֵׁב הַכָּתוּב נִתְּקוֹ לַעֲשֵׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the result of רבי שמעון's derivation for the question of lashes.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב חסדא's ruling of no מלקות follows רבי שמעון. The ברייתא that gives lashes follows רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Why is a זב more severe than a טמא מת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי שמעון assumed a זב is more severe than a טמא מת. It answers that the זב's impurity comes from his own body.
steps.simpleTranslation: What makes a זב more severe than someone impure from a dead body? His impurity comes out of his own body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back and checks the starting point of רבי שמעון's argument in step 12. It asks a question and gives a first answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's whole argument depends on the order of severity: טמא מת, then זב, then מצורע. If the זב is not clearly more severe, the קל וחומר falls apart. The first reason offered is that the זב's impurity comes from inside him, while a טמא מת got his impurity from something outside.

keyTerms.meaning: its stringency; what makes it more severe
a person impure from a dead body
comes out from his own body

phrases.english: What is the stringency of a zav over one impure from a corpse?
That impurity comes upon him from his own body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines the assumption behind רבי שמעון's קל וחומר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What makes a זב more severe than a טמא מת?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The זב's impurity comes from his own body.

steps.title: A טמא מת seems more severe because he needs sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. A טמא מת may actually be more severe, because he needs הזאה on the third and seventh days.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! A טמא מת is more severe, because he needs sprinkling on the third and seventh days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. It shows that the order of severity could go the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both impurities last seven days. Only the טמא מת needs sprinkling with the פרה אדומה waters, which makes him look more severe. If so, we cannot reason from טמא מת up to זב, and the word זב would no longer be extra.

keyTerms.meaning: on the contrary
sprinkling of the פרה אדומה waters
the third and seventh days

phrases.english: On the contrary: one impure from a corpse is more severe,
for he requires sprinkling on the third and seventh days.

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a זב is more severe than a טמא מת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only the טמא מת needs הזאה, so he is arguably more severe. Then the קל וחומר to זב fails.

steps.title: The verse includes a טמא שרץ, and a זב is clearly more severe than him
steps.stepSummary: The extra word וכל in וכל טמא includes a טמא שרץ among those sent out. A זב is clearly more severe than a טמא שרץ, so the קל וחומר works from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says not just 'impure' but 'and anyone impure.' This includes a person impure from a שרץ. And a זב is more severe than a person impure from a שרץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It changes the starting point of the קל וחומר from the טמא מת to a טמא שרץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We no longer need to compare the זב with the טמא מת. The verse itself includes the טמא שרץ in the rule of being sent out. Since a זב is clearly more severe than a טמא שרץ, a זב would be sent out anyway. So the word זב is still extra and still teaches a second camp.

keyTerms.meaning: to include
a person impure from touching a dead creeping creature

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not decide here whether a זב or a טמא מת is more severe. It simply goes around that question by using the טמא שרץ as the starting point.

phrases.english: The verse states not just 'impure' but 'and anyone impure',
phrases.notes: From במדבר ה:ב: וכל טמא לנפש.

phrases.english: to include one impure from a creeping creature.
And a zav is more severe than one impure from a creeping creature.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16 by changing the starting point of the קל וחומר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replaces the base of the קל וחומר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קל וחומר had to start from the טמא מת, who may be more severe than a זב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קל וחומר starts from the טמא שרץ, whom the verse includes, and who is less severe than a זב.

steps.title: How is a זב more severe than a טמא שרץ?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what makes a זב more severe than a טמא שרץ. It answers with the same reason as before: his impurity comes from his own body.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is his stringency? As we said before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the new assumption from step 17. It points back to the reason given in step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the 'from his own body' reason works without a counterweight like הזאה, because a טמא שרץ does not need sprinkling. This sets up the next challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: as we said before

phrases.english: And what is his stringency?
As we said: his impurity comes from his own body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the claim in step 17 that a זב is more severe than a טמא שרץ.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What makes a זב more severe than a טמא שרץ?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: His impurity comes from his own body, as stated in step 15.

steps.title: A שרץ may be more severe because it makes a person impure even by accident
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back again. A שרץ makes a person impure even באונס, while a זב is not impure if his discharge came from an outside cause. Then the גמרא introduces its reply with אמרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary! A שרץ is more severe, because it makes a person impure even by accident. They answered:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim that a זב is more severe than a טמא שרץ. The last word, אמרי, sets up the answer that comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב only becomes impure when the discharge is not caused by something outside, such as illness or certain foods. A שרץ makes a person impure no matter how the contact happened. So the שרץ could count as more severe, and the קל וחומר is in danger again.

keyTerms.meaning: a creeping creature (one of the eight in the Torah)
by accident; against one's will or because of an outside cause

phrases.english: On the contrary: a creeping creature is more severe,
for it makes a person impure even by accident!
phrases.notes: A זב whose discharge came from an outside cause is not impure as a זב.

phrases.english: They say in answer:
phrases.notes: This opens the answer, which continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּרַבָּה שֶׁרֶץ חָמוּר שֶׁכֵּן מְטַמֵּא בְּאוֹנֶס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 18, just as step 16 attacked step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a זב is more severe than a טמא שרץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A שרץ makes a person impure even באונס, which a זב's discharge does not. So the טמא שרץ may be more severe, and the קל וחומר to זב would fail again.
